night_8_9Feb.Japanese_action: Residual shelters and small groups conduct sniping, short ambushes, one mortar burst and two-to-four local break-out/infiltration attempts. Roughly 80-140 people are active over the night, but no more than about 30-50 act together at one time.
night_8_9Feb.US_response: US units maintain illumination plans, registered fires, roadblocks and tank/direct-fire stop lines while engineer/infantry sweep teams close bypassed shelters. Heavy naval fires are used sparingly because friendly lines now dominate the island.

morning_9Feb.clearance: Systematic shelter checks, demolitions and prisoner extraction continue. A few groups resist to destruction; others, especially wounded/support/labor personnel, are captured once isolated.
morning_9Feb.post_secure_residual: About 25-55 concealed individuals may remain after the declaration, but none form a mutually supporting combat system.

cumulative_main_ground_battles.scope: Roi-Namur plus Kwajalein ground/landing-area combat only. Excludes separate 5-Feb LST personnel losses, carrier-air exchange, naval and submarine casualties.

assessment: FLINTLOCK ground combat is operationally closed. Remaining danger is mopping-up/UXO/booby-trap exposure, not renewed organized defense.
